recipes.name: Cowboy Cookie Mix in a Jar

steps.text: Layer the ingredients in a 1-quart jar in the order given. Press each layer firmly in place before adding the next layer.

Include a card with the following instructions — Cowboy Cookie Mix in a Jar: 1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets. 2. In a medium bowl, mix together 1/2 cup melted butter or margarine, 1 egg, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla. Stir in the entire contents of the jar. You may need to use your hands to finish mixing. Shape into walnut-sized balls. Place 2 inches apart on prepared cookie sheets. 3. Bake for 11 to 13 minutes in the preheated oven. Transfer from cookie sheets to cool on wire racks.

review.reviewBody: Maybe the previous user cooked them too long or made them to small...these are great cookies, and very easy. My batch of 8 jars took about an hour to assemble. Found some cute red fabric at Walmart to glue on top of the jar and put these directions on my laser printer labels: Howdy Partner. Preheat your campfire to 350 and grease up your cornbread pan. You're in for a real sweet treat! Dump this jar into the biggest bowl ya got and mix it around real good. Add a stick of melted butter and whipped up egg. (A teaspoon of vanilla if you got some in the chuck wagon.) Mix with your five cleanest fingers till it looks like cookie dough ought to. Bake for 11-13 minutes. Makes 18 big 'ol cookies, or 2 dozen cowgirl-sized.

This was a really great recipe. I changed the arrangement of the ingredients putting the flour on bottom, then the oatmeal, brown sugar, white sugar, nuts (I used walnuts) and chocolate chips. This kept the flour from spilling into the nuts and chocolate chips. I was unable to use all of the chocolate chips but the cookies still turned out delicious. I used a small spice jar to press all of the layers into the jar. Several mentioned the cookies getting hard. If you will put a half slice of white bread (wheat may work, I've just never tried it) in the container with the cookies and put a lid on them, they will stay soft. The bread gets hard but the cookies stay soft...very weird. Anyway, I tied little inexpensive ornaments and ribbon around them and printed the instructions on decorative labels and put on the jars. TOO CUTE!!! These will make great gifts!!

Was so happy to find this recipe. I took the advice of others and just put in 3/4 cup chocolate chips and had to press down to make it all fit. The cookies were delicious but I got to thinking and realized that cowboy cookies are supposed to have coconut. I made a second jar, changing the order you stated so the flour was on the bottom, reduced the chocolate chips to 1/2 cup and and added 1/2 coconut. Still had to pack it tightly but a wide mouth mason jar worked better. They again were delicious but more of a traditional cowboy cookie. I will be giving them away this Christmas.

I can't find my previous review but I wanted to add these tips:

We used a wooden spoon to pack it down. 
Great family project. We made an assembly line. 
We used a large mouth funnel. 
There is more than enough room if you pack it down right. 
Do NOT follow the ingredients list. I started following the picture after reading reviews then found this to be best:
Flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt then oats, white sugar, brown sugar, nuts, chocolate chips. I even added more chocolate chips. 
The directions say, "walnut sized balls" but the dough thankfully didn't want to do that because they are much better maybe double that size. 
Some of the best cookies I have ever had!!!

This is a great recipe (had to test it out before giving it as gifts). 

For those who have had trouble fitting the contents into the jar, the following order of ingredients to go into the jar first is what worked for me:

1. Flour (using parchment paper to funnel into the mason jar)
2. Brown Sugar (then I patted down, which in turn compressed the flour underneath it, I also pressed some of the brown sugar against the side (1/2 C. isn't so much that you're going to get a thick looking layer unless you do this).
3. White Sugar
4. Oats
5. Baking Soda / Baking Powder
6. Chocolate Chips (the trick is to put in as much as you can (it won't be the full cup) and then press down on everything. It will compact all the layers underneath it. After that, you'll be able to pour the rest of the chocolate chip cookies in.

As you can see, I omitted the nuts. What I did was on the recipe instructions (where they add the butter, eggs and vanilla) is just added the instructions to add 1/2 C. chopped pecans if desired. That way you let the person who's receiving the gift decide if they want the nuts or not. 

Definitely a great, simple, (delicious), inexpensive & very thoughtful gift!

This was my first attempt at doing Cookies in a Jar. I made 9 total (neighbors, friends, teachers) and it took about an hour having an assembly line set up on my island. I omitted the nuts in case of allergies and everything fit just fine in the jars. I also used a piece of parchment paper rolled in a cone shape to get the ingredients in without making a mess. I layered them (bottom to top) - flour, salt, baking powder, soda, brown sugar, oats, white sugar, chocolate chips. I printed out instructions and glued to red cardstock, cut out with scrapbooking scissors, and tied to jars with pretty Christmas ribbon. I've not made them yet but the feedback so far is that they are delicious and easy! Friends and neighbors loved doing with kids. Great recipe. I'll post photo when I can.

I was easily able to fit all the ingredients using a 1L (33.8oz) wide-mouth Ball mason jar, and had 1" of space leftover. As others have noted, the ingredients are listed BACKWARDS. A few recommendations for all jarred cookie mixes: Flour/leavener goes on the bottom, followed by brown sugar and other dense ingredients, and topped with less dense "mix-ins". For ingredients in larger amounts (like flour), mound them in the center to make more room along the perimeter for the next layer. This will give you more defined layers.

The resulting cookie dough seemed too dry at first, but eventually came together just fine. I used 1.5Tbs scoops and baked the first batch for 11 min, pulling them when the centers were soft and the edges were barely crisp. They had great flavor, shape, & texture. However, after cooling, these cookies went from chewy to rock hard, moreso than other cookie recipes. I underbaked the second batch, and that seemed to do the trick.

EDIT* I just put a jar of this mix together and everything fit perfectly! I used the back of a large stirring spoon to pack everything down*EDIT
This was amazing! I tried out this recipe yesterday and I'll definitely be putting it in jars for Christmas gifts in the next few weeks. I took out the walnuts and only had about 3/4 c of mini chocolate chips on hand but that seemed to be plenty. I also had trouble with the dough being too dry so I added a 2nd egg and cooked them for about 8-10 minutes and they were perfect! Husband I can't stop eating them! Thanks for this awesome recipe, besides the extra egg and a shorter cook time I wouldn't change a thing!

Like others I decided I need to rearrange the layers and probly decrease the oats and chocolate chips slightly for an easier fit. And put flour on bottom. I added 1 extra egg as someone else suggested as well as some cinnamon. Turned out greAt. Will be making jars for coworkers.

I made this as a Christmas gift this year for my mom and MIL and since I had all the ingredients already out, I decided to make a batch for myself to test it out and these cookies are SO GOOD. The batter did seem a little dry to me, so I might recommend for them to add a tablespoon of butter or milk to it to help hold the cookies together a bit better, but other than that, this recipe is definitely a keeper! I was able to easily fit all my ingredients into the jars by pressing down hard on each layer before adding the next one and I mixed the brown and white sugar together to make one layer.

These are fabulous cookies.... I had to reduce the oats to 1 1/4, chips to 1/2 and nuts to 1/3 only because I used old mason jars with glass tops with wire latches (not ones with screw on lids) and they must be smaller because I couldn't fit everything as here. After making those adjustments they fit perfect. But nonetheless I wanted to make them to see what I was giving away and to find out what they tasted like. One of the best cookies I have made in a while. Thank you!! Cooked for 11 mins and they turned out a chewy golden brown. Oh and I recommend using margarine not butter, I used smart balance, real butter tends to make cookies crispy/dry.

I've been making these cookies and teaching my kids, and nephews and nieces to make them for a long time now. I teach them to just dump it in a gallon freezer bag and pull it out and make them when they want cookies. Always a big hit with my family. If I want a cowboy cookie, this is the recipe I'm craving. Good job, Phyllis.
We didn’t make it right away, needed to get fresh brown sugar because it hardened in the jar. Other than that it turned out ok! A little crumbly but still delicious.

I gave this 4 stars because I have not baked them and made them for gifts, so not sure how they will mix up, bake, and taste. After reading reviews I made a paper funnel and dropped flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in first, then oats. I tamped this down with back flat side of my candy thermometer. Added brown sugar, tamped some more, white sugar, tamped, flour, tamped, and finally chocolate chips. I could not fit nuts in and that’s ok. I used a wide mouth one quart jar. I wish now I would have added a half teaspoon of cinnamon. Makes a very nice presentation. I made several for gifts.

Awesome recipe and concept. Don’t listen to people about this not fitting in the jar, it does! Use a wide mouth mason jar for easier packing and use the right method for measuring your dry ingredients, loosely packing in the measuring cup, not packing the measuring cup tightly.

It doesn't matter how much I would press the stuff down, not all the ingredients fit! I had to dump it out and start over with a different recipe. Total waste of time and ingredients, now I'm trying to figure out what to do with the mix I have.

My son gave me a jar as a gift. I didn't try making the cookies for over 2 years. When I did make the cookies, they didn't melt down, and the dough was very dry. I believe the brown sugar dried out, etc., making it hard for the egg and butter and vanilla to do their work. However, I'm making the next batch with a little more butter added and we'll see. The flavor, however, is AWESOME, and the concept is fun and welcome! I'm going to try making several jars of the cookie mix as gifts.

No way this all fits in a quart jar. Of course it wasn't realized until it was time to add the flour. I will be making 12 batches of cookies to gift instead of presenting jars. Frustrating to say the least!
For those who haven't yet assembled them, try moving the flour and oats to add as your bottom layer, then you can adjust the other ingredients as needed.
The recipe and cookies are great.... however, the ingredients won’t fit in the size jar it recommends. It needs a bigger jar!
They are awesome!
